application.product: Memos — an open-source, self-hosted personal knowledge base for lightweight notes ('memos'), backed by a SQLite file
application.frontend: Vite 2 React single-page application under web/, TypeScript, with a hand-rolled two-entry router and a dialog-driven UI
application.backend: A Go HTTP server in the SAME repository at the repository root (35 .go files, echo + SQLite). It is OUT of this fixture's build scope and was neither built nor run. The frontend reaches it same-origin over /api/*; the Vite dev server proxies /api and /h/ to http://localhost:8080.
application.router: none — a hand-rolled 20-line router with two entries: "/signin" and "*" (Home)
application.state: @reduxjs/toolkit ^1.8.1 with five slices (editor, location, memo, shortcut, user), react-redux ^8.0.1, plus a hand-written service layer under src/services
application.http: axios ^0.27.2 with withCredentials = true against same-origin /api
application.markdown: a hand-rolled renderer in src/helpers/marked.ts (no markdown library in the closure)
application.notableInternals: src/labs/html2image — a hand-rolled DOM-to-image implementation used by the share-memo-as-image dialog

node.honestLabel: era-consistent, NOT repository-pinned. The repository pins Node 14.18.2; this baseline ran on Node 16.20.2. Node 14 has no darwin-arm64 build at all — official darwin-arm64 binaries begin at Node 16 — so honouring 14.18.2 on this host would require Rosetta 2 (which would also force the x64 esbuild binary) or a linux container. Node 16 is inside the era policy for the Vite 2.9 line (Node 14/16) and is the oldest natively-runnable Node here.

legacyCell.lifecycleScriptsCaveat: esbuild 0.14.36 needs its install.js to link its platform binary. With scripts disabled, any later unit must bootstrap esbuild before the bundler will run.
legacyCell.rationale: The repository's own declared cell is honoured as closely as this host allows: its committed yarn v1 lockfile is used verbatim under --frozen-lockfile, its declared build command is run unmodified, and only the Node major is raised 14 -> 16 for the platform reason recorded above.

lockState.searchScope: the full recursive git tree at the pinned revision (205 blobs)
lockState.consequence: The dependency closure IS pinned by the repository and yarn accepted --frozen-lockfile, so nothing was re-resolved against today's registry. The build outcome recorded below is therefore a property of the pinned revision, not of the 2026 registry. This is the strongest lock state in the corpus so far.

baseline.installDetail: yarn 1.22.19 installed the committed lockfile's 347 entries (331 package directories, 26 of them nested) in 4 seconds on Node 16.20.2, with --frozen-lockfile accepted and lifecycle scripts disabled.
baseline.buildDetail: `yarn build` (`tsc && vite build`) exited 2 inside the tsc gate, before the bundler ran. Four errors, all in node_modules and none under src: TS2300 duplicate identifier 'LibraryManagedAttributes' and two TS2717 subsequent-property-declaration errors. Cause: web/yarn.lock pins TWO copies of @types/react — 18.0.9 top-level and 18.0.5 nested under @types/react-dom@18.0.4 (whose range is `@types/react "*"`) — while web/tsconfig.json sets "skipLibCheck": false. This is not registry drift; both versions come from the repository's own lockfile.

bundlerObservation.what: esbuild's suppressed postinstall was run to link its lockfile-pinned platform binary, then `vite build` was invoked alone, skipping the tsc gate.

journeyShapeCaveat: This application has only two routes ("/signin" and "*"). Its journeys are dialog- and state-driven inside a single Home page, not route-driven. Any later witness work must drive them through UI state rather than URL navigation.
knownRisks: The declared build command does not succeed at this revision: `tsc` fails on a duplicate @types/react pinned twice by the repository's own lockfile under "skipLibCheck": false. Any build lane for this fixture must confront that gate rather than route around it silently.

The frontend cannot run without the Go backend. There is no client-side persistence and no mock layer; axios sends credentials to same-origin /api, and Home.tsx redirects to /signin unless a session is established. No user journey is exercisable until the Go backend (Go toolchain, out of this ingest's scope) is running or the /api surface is stubbed.
The Go backend lives in the same repository but is out of this fixture's build scope. It was neither built nor run, and its behavior is not established here.
esbuild's platform binary depends on a lifecycle script that the baseline install suppressed; it must be bootstrapped before the bundler runs in any --ignore-scripts cell.
